intended_object: A bookkeeping helper for the two-pole gluing criterion in chip-firing. Given a divisor D on a graph with two marked poles p₁, p₂ and integer "fluxes" c₁, c₂, it returns D − c₁·[p₁] − c₂·[p₂]. This comes from the docstring and from how the module uses it in IsDebitResponse and the gluing theorems.
explanation:
The body is `D - c₁ • oneChip p.first - c₂ • oneChip p.second`. Here `oneChip v` is the indicator divisor of the vertex v, so the body is exactly D − c₁·p₁ − c₂·p₂. This matches the docstring ("debit the two boundary fluxes"), and `deg_debit` confirms that the degree drops by c₁ + c₂.

The definition is not a standard notion from the literature. It is an auxiliary device that packages the boundary correction used to state `IsDebitResponse` and to prove the exact two-pole gluing criterion (`winnable_sumDivisor_iff_exists_responses`). The bookkeeping itself is correct, including when p₁ = p₂: the two corrections then add up at the same vertex, which is what the gluing proof needs.

It is also not too narrow. The divisor group of a chip-firing graph is the natural setting, and Mathlib has no matching notion. So this is an internal construction, not a mathematical object to compare with the literature.
